criterios: This question resolves YES if the market-capitalization rank shown for Zcash (ZEC) on its CoinGecko coin page (https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/zcash) is 10 or better (i.e., any value from 1 through 10) as of the end of October 15, 2026 (23:59 UTC). It resolves NO if the displayed rank is 11 or worse at that time. The rank is the value shown in CoinGecko's "#" (Rank) field, which reflects its default all-cryptocurrencies ranking by market cap (this ranking includes stablecoins and every asset CoinGecko lists in that table). For example, a displayed rank of 9 resolves YES and a displayed rank of 12 resolves NO.
letra_pequena: The rank field on the CoinGecko Zcash page (https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/zcash) is authoritative. If both sources display a rank and they disagree, the CoinGecko value controls.

**(a) Time left:** About 10.3 days, from Oct 5 to 23:59 UTC on Oct 15, 2026.

**(b) Status quo:** ZEC is #10 on CoinGecko at $21.9B. That is about 5.8% ahead of #11 HYPE ($20.7B). DOGE is far behind at #12. If nothing changes, the answer is YES.

**(c) Reference class:** A highly volatile asset that holds a small lead (about 6%) over its nearest rival for 10 days. The ZEC/HYPE ratio has a 10-day standard deviation of roughly 15–20%, an estimate rather than a computed figure. With no drift, the chance that the ratio falls more than 5.8% is about 35–38%. That gives a baseline of about 62–65% for YES. ZEC and HYPE have already swapped places at least twice in the past month, so the rivalry is clearly unstable.

**Adjustments:**
- **HYPE unlock:** About 9.9M HYPE (roughly 4.5% of supply) vests on Oct 6. If CoinGecko adds it to circulating supply, the cushion shrinks to about 1.5%. CoinGecko did not update after the Sep 6 unlock, so I put this at maybe 30–40% likely.
- **Momentum:** It favours HYPE. ZEC is down 15.6% over 7 days, its ETF had its first net-outflow week, and there is whale selling. HYPE is near its all-time high, with buybacks and an OTC sale that keeps tokens off the open market. Short-term momentum in crypto is only weakly predictive, but it tilts the odds slightly toward NO.
- **Upside for ZEC:** There are some catalysts, such as the Grayscale institutional pitch and NU7 hype before the Nov 5 fork.

**(d) NO scenario:** ETF outflows continue and ZEC slides to about $1,150–1,200. Meanwhile HYPE pushes to a new all-time high above $98, or CoinGecko adds the unlocked supply. HYPE passes ZEC and ZEC shows #11 on Oct 15.

**(e) YES scenario:** ZEC stabilises or rebounds into the $1,300–1,500 range on pre-NU7 positioning and institutional interest. HYPE consolidates below its all-time high and CoinGecko's supply figure stays stale. ZEC remains #10, or even #9.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- Only CoinGecko's displayed rank at 23:59 UTC on Oct 15 counts. CoinMarketCap already shows HYPE ahead of ZEC, but it is only the fallback source.
- FIGR_HELOC holds #9 on CoinGecko. If it were delisted or reclassified, ZEC would move up one place, which would help YES, but that seems unlikely.
- A HYPE supply update on CoinGecko is the main risk that could decide the outcome on its own.

Netting these out: a baseline of about 63%, lowered for the unlock risk and the adverse momentum, lands around 53%.

Probability: 53%
